paper_title: Bounds on Axions-Like Particles Shining in the Ultra-Violet
notes: Paper constrains ALP-photon coupling g_agamma using HST archival UV spectroscopy (110-170 nm) of dwarf spheroidal galaxies (Ursa Minor, Draco) and galaxy clusters (Virgo, Fornax). The main result is shown in Figure 3 (right panel, combined limit). The paper states the derived limit 'excludes values above 10^-12 GeV^-1 over the whole mass range' and 'reaching g_agamma < 2 × 10^-13 GeV for some masses.' The mass range is 14.4-22.2 eV. Data points extracted from abstract and conclusions: the upper envelope is ~10^-12 GeV^-1 across the range, with the best limit reaching ~2×10^-13 GeV^-1 at intermediate masses. Figure 3 shows the combined bound as a band with thickness representing D-factor uncertainty. The two-point representation at mass boundaries (14.4 and 22.2 eV) with coupling 10^-12 GeV^-1 represents the conservative (upper) limit stated in the abstract; the second pair at 2×10^-13 GeV^-1 represents the best achieved limit mentioned in the abstract. This is a measured exclusion limit (95% C.L.) from HST observations, not a projection. The paper does not assume a specific local DM density for these astrophysical targets—instead it uses measured D-factors (line-of-sight integrals of DM density) from the literature for each target. Confidence is high because the coupling type is unambiguous (ALP-photon coupling g_agamma explicitly stated throughout) and the numerical limits are clearly stated in abstract and text, though the exact shape of the exclusion curve in Figure 3 is not tabulated numerically. | selector: text over figure_vision (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 3, 0, 0.85, 4))
